nodes.content: Develop an image segmentation model that distinguishes genuine boundary ambiguity from unfamiliar anatomy under acquisition-domain shift.
requirements: Achieve unfamiliar-anatomy detection AUROC ≥0.85 on held-out acquisition domains.
Achieve boundary-uncertainty Spearman correlation ≥0.6 with inter-annotator disagreement while matching a supervised baseline’s Dice.

nodes.content: Train acquisition-augmented segmentation using Dice supervision, annotator-calibrated boundary entropy, and acquisition-invariant shape-latent novelty scoring.
Does shape-latent novelty remain anatomy-specific when low-contrast edges inflate boundary entropy on unseen scanners?
On held-out scanners, shape-latent novelty distinguishes unfamiliar anatomy from low-contrast normal boundaries with AUROC ≥0.85.
On held-out ShiftHeart scanners, compare shape-latent novelty and boundary-entropy AUROC for congenital variants versus low-contrast normal hearts.
On held-out ShiftHeart scanners, shape-latent novelty achieved AUROC 0.88 versus boundary entropy’s 0.62 for congenital variants versus low-contrast normals.
Select shape-latent novelty over boundary entropy for unfamiliar-anatomy detection, based on ShiftHeart AUROC of 0.88 versus 0.62.
Retain shape-latent novelty; calibrate boundary entropy using multi-rater masks, then evaluate independent-domain AUROC, disagreement Spearman ρ, and baseline-relative Dice.
Calibrate boundary entropy with ShiftHeart multi-rater masks; measure disagreement Spearman ρ and baseline-relative Dice on unseen scanners.
ShiftHeart boundary-calibration report containing multi-rater disagreement maps, unseen-scanner Spearman ρ, and Dice comparisons against the supervised baseline.
Audit the ShiftHeart report’s scanner-stratified disagreement maps and verify Spearman ρ≥0.6 without Dice loss versus the supervised baseline.
ShiftHeart unseen scanners yielded boundary-entropy disagreement Spearman ρ=0.66 and Dice 0.89, matching the supervised baseline’s 0.89.
Using ShiftHeart-validated boundary calibration, test novelty–ambiguity gating on external CardioMRI-X scanners for anatomy AUROC, disagreement ρ, and Dice.
CardioMRI-X evaluation bundle with scanner-stratified anatomy AUROC, boundary-disagreement Spearman ρ, Dice, and novelty–ambiguity gating outputs.
Does novelty–ambiguity gating preserve boundary-disagreement calibration when unfamiliar anatomy has low-contrast contours on CardioMRI-X?
On low-contrast CardioMRI-X variants, novelty–ambiguity gating preserves disagreement Spearman ρ≥0.6 and matches the supervised baseline’s Dice.
Evaluate gated versus ungated predictions on low-contrast CardioMRI-X variants using multi-rater boundary-disagreement Spearman ρ and baseline-relative Dice.
On low-contrast CardioMRI-X variants, gating reduced disagreement Spearman ρ from 0.63 to 0.44 and Dice to 0.86 versus baseline 0.88.
Replace novelty–ambiguity gating with independent, stop-gradient shape-novelty and annotator-calibrated boundary heads, reporting both scores without suppressing either.
Using the CardioMRI-X bundle, compare p1’s acquisition-augmented entropy/novelty model with p2’s independent stop-gradient heads on AUROC, disagreement ρ, and Dice.
CardioMRI-X: gated p1 versus p2 achieved AUROC 0.86/0.88, disagreement ρ 0.44/0.65, Dice 0.86/0.88 (baseline 0.88).
Is p2’s 0.88 AUROC driven by congenital-anatomy morphology rather than scanner-specific intensity signatures in CardioMRI-X?
Under scanner-style swaps, p2 retains anatomy AUROC ≥0.85, while morphology-shuffled controls fall below 0.70.
Following p2’s CardioMRI-X AUROC 0.88, measure AUROC after structure-preserving scanner-style swaps and morphology-code shuffling with scanner intensities preserved.
CardioMRI-X p2 AUROC fell from 0.88 to 0.77 after scanner-style swaps; morphology-code shuffling yielded 0.59.
Scanner intensity partly contaminates p2’s shape latent; scanner-adversarial training will restore style-swap AUROC ≥0.85 while morphology-shuffled AUROC remains <0.70.
Retrain p2’s shape latent with gradient-reversal scanner classification; compare CardioMRI-X style-swap and morphology-shuffle AUROCs against original p2.
Scanner-adversarial p2 raised CardioMRI-X style-swap AUROC from 0.77 to 0.86; morphology-shuffled AUROC remained 0.60.
Adopt scanner-adversarial independent heads without novelty–ambiguity gating: style-swap AUROC reached 0.86, whereas gating reduced boundary ρ to 0.44.
Validate adopted scanner-adversarial independent heads on untouched scanners using multi-rater masks: anatomy AUROC ≥0.85, disagreement ρ≥0.6, baseline-matched Dice.
Use ShiftHeart calibration maps to freeze boundary-head temperature; assess anatomy AUROC, disagreement ρ, and Dice on untouched OpenHeart-3 scanners.
OpenHeart-3 validation dossier with frozen boundary temperature, scanner-stratified anatomy AUROC, multi-rater disagreement ρ, and baseline-relative Dice.
Use scanner-normalized anatomical prototype distances for novelty and a multi-rater contour ensemble for boundary uncertainty, preserving Dice-supervised segmentation.
Can scanner-normalized anatomical prototypes detect congenital variants absent from training without labeling disputed normal contours as unfamiliar?
Using OpenHeart-3 dossier labels, compare p3 prototype versus p1 shape-latent novelty on congenital-variant AUROC and disputed-normal-contour false-positive rates.
OpenHeart-3: p3 prototypes achieved AUROC 0.87, disputed-contour FPR 6%; p1’s ungated shape latent achieved AUROC 0.90, FPR 15%.
Select p3 novelty over p1’s higher-AUROC latent for its 6% versus 15% disputed-contour FPR; retain p2’s independent boundary head.
Validate selected prototypes on held-out scanner–variant pairs, targeting congenital-variant AUROC ≥0.85 and disputed-contour false-positive rate ≤10%.
Run leave-one-scanner–variant-pair-out validation on OpenHeart-3, measuring prototype novelty AUROC and disputed-contour FPR at a prespecified threshold.
Revised OpenHeart-3 dossier adds leave-one-scanner–variant-pair-out prototype AUROC and prespecified-threshold disputed-contour FPR to prior validation metrics.
Audit revised OpenHeart-3 dossier for per-pair prototype AUROC ≥0.85 and disputed-contour FPR ≤10% at the prespecified threshold.
OpenHeart-3 leave-one-scanner–variant-pair-out validation yielded minimum prototype AUROC 0.85 and maximum disputed-contour FPR 9%.
On low-contrast CardioMRI-X variants, ungated prototypes and contour ensembles retain disagreement ρ≥0.6, anatomy AUROC≥0.85, and baseline-matched Dice≥0.88.
Test ungated p3 on low-contrast CardioMRI-X variants, measuring anatomy AUROC, contour-disagreement Spearman ρ, and Dice against baseline.
Low-contrast CardioMRI-X: AUROC 0.86, disagreement ρ=0.62, Dice 0.88 (baseline 0.88), but disputed-normal-contour FPR reached 24%.
Apply contrast-stratified conformal thresholds to p3 prototype novelty, calibrated on disputed normal contours while keeping boundary ensembles independent.
Calibrate p4 thresholds on separate low-contrast normal contours, then validate FPR ≤10%, AUROC ≥0.85, ρ≥0.6, and baseline-matched Dice.
Using CardioMRI-X bundle scanner labels, fit contrast-stratified conformal prototype thresholds on a separate disputed-normal calibration split.
CardioMRI-X contrast-stratified conformal threshold file with calibration split identifiers, prototype-score quantiles, and scanner-independent threshold settings.
Audit r5’s CardioMRI-X calibration split against r4’s OpenHeart-3 pairs; measure frozen-threshold disputed-contour FPR and variant sensitivity.
On held-out low-contrast CardioMRI-X, conformal thresholds reduced disputed-contour FPR from 24% to 8% at 83% variant sensitivity.
Adopt contrast-stratified thresholds provisionally: CardioMRI-X FPR fell to 8% at 83% sensitivity, complementing OpenHeart-3’s ≤9% pairwise FPR.
With provisionally adopted thresholds frozen, evaluate p4 on untouched OpenHeart-4 scanners: novelty AUROC, disputed-contour FPR, boundary ρ, and baseline-relative Dice.
On untouched OpenHeart-4, p4 yielded anatomy AUROC 0.82 and disputed-contour FPR 18%; disagreement ρ=0.63, Dice 0.88.
Did prototype-score drift or contrast-bin misassignment drive OpenHeart-4’s 18% disputed-contour FPR and 0.82 AUROC?
Normal-contour prototype scores shift upward on OpenHeart-4; oracle contrast bins leave disputed-contour FPR >10% and anatomy AUROC <0.85.
Investigate OpenHeart-4 failures by comparing normal-score distributions with calibration and recomputing p4 FPR/AUROC under oracle contrast bins.
OpenHeart-4 normal prototype-score median rose from calibration’s 0.31 to 0.49; oracle contrast bins left FPR 16% and AUROC 0.83.
Revoke frozen-threshold adoption; revive drift-aware p4: CardioMRI-X AUROC 0.86/ρ=0.62 persisted despite OpenHeart-4 normal-score median shifting 0.31→0.49.
